name: Slow Cooker Salsa Verde Pork Bowls
intro_html: Salsa verde does the heavy lifting here, so you get bright, tangy pork with almost no effort. It stacks up {{protein}} grams of protein per bowl over rice and corn, all for right around ${{cost_ps}} a serving (at everyday cost). Fourteen servings from one batch is a whole lot of lunch for the money.
ingredients_display: Diced Green Chiles (Old El Paso): 8 tbsp (120 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 4 1/2 cups (750 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Rice, 5.25 cups dry: ~$1.16. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 2lb bags.
Diced Green Chiles, 8 tbsp: ~$1.06. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 4oz cans.
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn, 4 1/2 cups: ~$1.06. Buy 2 cans: $1.22.
Chicken Broth, 2 cups: ~$0.73. Buy 1 (covers about two batches).
Pantry seasonings (salt): ~$0.01. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $36.16 across 14 servings, so roughly $2.58 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $39.64 across 14 servings, roughly $2.83 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $5.83 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $45.47. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
shop_smart: Pork tenderloin runs lean and clean, but watch the tag. If the per-pound price is steep, check for pork loin instead and save real money on the same batch.
A single jar of salsa verde does most of the seasoning, so you skip buying a handful of separate spices.
Buy lime juice in a bottle rather than fresh limes for batch cooking. It keeps in the fridge and you only use a splash.
make_it: Set the pork tenderloin in the slow cooker.
Pour the salsa verde, diced green chiles, and chicken broth over the top, then stir in the brown sugar and a little salt.
Add a squeeze of lime juice and the minced garlic.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork pulls apart easily.
Shred the pork and stir it back into all those juices, then fold in the corn.
Spoon over cooked white rice and divide into containers.
portion_html: You are looking at about {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein in every serving.
